original_value: Providing model-generated explanations in recommender systems is important to user experience. State-of-the-art recommendation algorithms—especially the collaborative filtering (CF)- based approaches with shallow or deep models—usually work with various unstructured information sources for recommendation, such as textual reviews, visual images, and various implicit or explicit feedbacks. Though structured knowledge bases were considered in content-based approaches, they have been largely ignored recently due to the availability of vast amounts of data and the learning power of many complex models. However, structured knowledge bases exhibit unique advantages in personalized recommendation systems. When the explicit knowledge about users and items is considered for recommendation, the system could provide highly customized recommendations based on users’ historical behaviors and the knowledge is helpful for providing informed explanations regarding the recommended items. A great challenge for using knowledge bases for recommendation is how to integrate large-scale structured and unstructured data, while taking advantage of collaborative filtering for highly accurate performance. Recent achievements in knowledge-base embedding (KBE) sheds light on this problem, which makes it possible to learn user and item representations while preserving the structure of their relationship with external knowledge for explanation. In this work, we propose to explain knowledge-base embeddings for explainable recommendation. Specifically, we propose a knowledge-base representation learning framework to embed heterogeneous entities for recommendation, and based on the embedded knowledge base, a soft matching algorithm is proposed to generate personalized explanations for the recommended items. Experimental results on real-world e-commerce datasets verified the superior recommendation performance and the explainability power of our approach compared with state-of-the-art baselines.

result.paraphrase: Generating model-produced explanations is important for user experience in recommender systems. State-of-the-art recommendation methods, particularly collaborative filtering (CF) approaches with shallow or deep models, typically rely on diverse unstructured information sources such as textual reviews, visual images, and implicit or explicit feedback. Although structured knowledge bases were once used in content-based approaches, they have recently been largely overlooked because of the abundance of data and the learning capacity of many complex models. Even so, structured knowledge bases offer distinctive advantages in personalized recommendation systems. By incorporating explicit knowledge about users and items, a system can deliver highly tailored recommendations based on users’ historical behavior, and this knowledge also helps produce informed explanations for recommended items. A major challenge in using knowledge bases for recommendation is integrating large-scale structured and unstructured data while still leveraging collaborative filtering for highly accurate performance. Recent advances in knowledge-base embedding (KBE) provide a solution by making it possible to learn user and item representations while preserving relationship structure with external knowledge for explanation. In this work, we propose explaining knowledge-base embeddings for explainable recommendation. Specifically, we present a knowledge-base representation learning framework that embeds heterogeneous entities for recommendation, and then use the embedded knowledge base with a soft matching algorithm to generate personalized explanations for recommended items. Experiments on real-world e-commerce datasets show that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both recommendation performance and explainability.
